page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system integrates 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that delivers high memory density for low-core workloads.

Managed through a KVM hypervisor, the server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The configuration excludes dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and provides no local storage drives, which shifts all I/O demands and persistent data retention to attached network storage.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio minimizes unnecessary compute capacity while allocating ample RAM for memory-constrained tasks. Operational tradeoffs include the lack of ephemeral local high-speed storage and entry-level network throughput. Primary workload fits include in-memory key-value data stores, distributed caching layers, small relational databases, and memory-intensive background processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.large is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8475B processor built on x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Virtualized via KVM, the instance features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, contains zero GPUs, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There is no bundled local storage, requiring persistent data to reside on external block storage services. This hardware configuration enables resource-efficient deployment of memory-heavy applications without paying for excess compute cores. The architecture suits lightweight in-memory databases, key-value caches like Redis, ETL buffer pipelines, and small memory-bound enterprise applications.
